First release of **uun**, a universal update notifier. It's a terminal UI that runs updates across all your package managers and keeps track of when the software on your system reaches end-of-life.

## Highlights

- **One place for updates:** apt, dnf/yum, zypper, pacman, flatpak, snap, Homebrew, pip (user/venv only), pipx, cargo, rustup and npm, with pending and security update counts. Every update shows the exact commands for you to confirm before anything runs.
- **End-of-life tracking:** the OS, kernel, runtimes, databases and web servers, checked against [endoflife.date](https://endoflife.date) data that's refreshed daily by a systemd user timer.
- **Alternatives when software reaches end-of-life with no fix on the way:** for example MySQL → MariaDB, Redis → Valkey, CentOS → Rocky/Alma, Terraform → OpenTofu, with install hints for your distro.
- **tmux-style themes** (`set -g status-style …`, `bind-key`, `source-file`); 6 bundled, switchable live with `t`. Upper-right ISO 8601 clock.
- **Report mode** for cron and CI: `uun --report [--json]`. Exit codes: 0 = all OK, 1 = something needs attention, 2 = something is past end-of-life.

## Security

This release includes the fixes from a pre-release security audit. All findings scoring CVSS 3.1 ≥ 4.0 are fixed, as are the lower-scored ones. Details are in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/nc-intezra/uun/blob/v0.1.0/SECURITY.md) (#1).

- Child processes run with `cwd=/`, so a hostile folder you launch uun from can't inject code.
- Programs are only taken from trusted `PATH` directories, and `sudo` must be a root-owned setuid binary.
- Config files that define commands run with sudo are checked for safe ownership and permissions before they're read, in a way that can't be raced.
- EoL data is strictly validated, and anything displayed is stripped of control characters and shown as plain text.
- Bundled dependencies are pinned by hash and pip-audited, with no known CVEs.

## Packages

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `uun_0.1.0-1_all.deb` | Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 12 / 13, Raspberry Pi OS bookworm+ (arm64 and armhf) |
| `uun-0.1.0-1.noarch.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL / Rocky / Alma 9 (installs `python3.11`+ automatically), openSUSE Leap 15.6 |
| `uun-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`, `uun-0.1.0.tar.gz` | `pipx install` / pip on any Linux with Python ≥ 3.11 |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums for all of the above |

Each package was install-tested in clean containers of every distro listed above, including arm64 and armhf (Raspberry Pi) under emulation. The tests ran as an unprivileged user, used the live end-of-life data, and removed the package cleanly afterwards.

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing

# Ubuntu / Debian / Raspberry Pi OS
sudo apt install ./uun_0.1.0-1_all.deb
# Fedora / RHEL / Rocky / Alma
sudo dnf install ./uun-0.1.0-1.noarch.rpm
# openSUSE Leap
sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./uun-0.1.0-1.noarch.rpm

systemctl --user enable --now uun-eol-refresh.timer   # daily end-of-life data refresh
uun --demo                                            # safe preview on sample data
uun
```

## Requirements and known limitations

- **Python 3.11 or newer.** Ubuntu 22.04 and Raspberry Pi OS bullseye ship 3.10 and 3.9; there, use pipx with a newer Python.
- **Packages aren't GPG-signed yet.** Check them against `SHA256SUMS` from this release page.
- **Builds are reproducible:** `packaging/build.sh` rebuilds byte-identical packages from the same tag.
